en: "Oṃ"—this syllable is all this; its further explanation is as follows: whatever has been, whatever is, and whatever will be—all that is indeed the syllable Oṃ.
And whatever else transcends the three periods of time, that too is indeed the syllable Oṃ.
For all this is indeed Brahman; this Self is Brahman. This very Self has four quarters.
The first quarter is Vaiśvānara, whose sphere is the waking state, who perceives external objects, who has seven limbs and nineteen mouths, and who experiences gross objects.
The second quarter is Taijasa, whose departure is from within, who is conscious of internal objects, who has seven limbs and nineteen mouths, and who experiences subtle objects. MandU 4.
That state where one who is asleep desires no desire whatsoever and sees no dream—that is deep sleep (*suṣupta*).

In the state of deep sleep, having become unified, he is indeed a mass of consciousness, consisting of bliss, an enjoyer of bliss, whose face is the mind; this is the third quarter, the Wise One (*prājña*). (MandU 5)
He is the Lord of all, He is the All-knowing, He is the Inner Controller, He is the source of all; for He is the origin and the dissolution of all beings.

They consider the Fourth (the *turiya*) to be neither conscious of the internal, nor conscious of the external, nor conscious of both, nor a mass of consciousness, nor consciousness, nor non-consciousness; unseen, beyond conventional usage, ungraspable, without characteristics, unthinkable, indescribable, whose essence is the realization of the one Self, the cessation of the manifold, peaceful, auspicious, and non-dual;
that is the Self, and that is what is to be known.
This very Self is the imperishable syllable *oṃ*.
Its parts are the measures (*mātrā*), and the measures are the parts: the letter *a*, the letter *u*, and the letter *m*. (MandU 8)

Vaiśvānara, whose sphere is the waking state, is the letter *a*, the first measure, because of attainment (*āpti*) or because of being the beginning (*āditva*). He who knows this indeed attains all desires and becomes the beginning. (MandU 9)
The Taijasa, abiding in the state of dream, is the letter *U*, the second *mātrā*, because of its excellence or because it stands between both.
Indeed, it causes the continuity of knowledge to excel,
and one becomes equal [to all].
In the family of one who knows this, there is no one who does not know Brahman. MandU 10.
The state of deep sleep is the wise one (prājña), the letter *m*, the third measure; it is so called because of measuring (*miti*) or because of merging (*apīti*).
Indeed, he who knows this measures all this and becomes the merger.
The fourth is without measure, beyond conventional discourse, the cessation of phenomenal proliferation, auspicious, and non-dual.
Thus, the syllable Om is indeed the Self.
He who knows this enters the Self by means of the Self.
